4a60a30ffd63.en: How do I price a BOQ in I-Cost?

2eeb6dfeb625.en: Import the client's BOQ from Excel or CSV, check it against the total, add cost rates from your library or past jobs, apply the margin and send the quotation PDF. Copied rates are checked against what you have bought since.

2fc8321c5b7b.en: Can I import my client's Excel BOQ?

070e209d4640.en: Yes. Upload the Excel or CSV file, tell I-Cost what each column is, check the preview and the total, and bring the lines straight into the estimate. Nobody has to retype it.

5f768a17cdee.en: Can I do quantity takeoff in I-Cost?

94a2d572916c.en: Yes, from a BIM model: import an IFC file exported from Revit, ArchiCAD, Tekla or similar, and I-Cost adds up the quantities, keeping the levels, in the same preview as a BOQ import. In Revit 2023 to 2027 the free <1>I-Cost Model Link</1> add-in sends them straight from the model.

47546eb8deb1.en: Can AI estimate my construction project?

fdbd843f9bdc.en: A chatbot on its own does not know what you pay. I-Cost keeps your real supplier quotes and purchase order prices next to the estimate, and its AI guide prices start from those, show where each figure came from and change nothing until you press Use. <1>Why real prices matter</1>.

4e9f54a517bf.en: Is it suitable for subcontractors pricing a package?

43c27a80f0f7.en: Yes. Specialist and trade subcontractors import the main contractor's BOQ for their package, price it and send their quotation in the same way.
